question: What is the maximum number of words permitted on every static regulatory or warning sign?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence provided does not contain any provision establishing a maximum number of words permitted on static regulatory or warning signs. The only message-length limitation in the evidence applies to changeable message signs (CMS), which are limited by phases and lines of text, not by a word count, and that provision does not apply to static signs. The evidence is insufficient to answer the question as asked. Standards (mandatory): - For changeable message signs only (not static signs): "Each message shall consist of no more than two phases. A phase shall consist of no more than three lines of text. Each phase shall be understood by itself, and the meaning of the entire message shall be the same, regardless of the sequence in which the phases are read." This does not establish a word limit for static regulatory or warning signs. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-1 shows methods of enhancing sign conspicuity (plaques, flags, beacons, LEDs) but contains no word-count rule; [Image 2] Figure 6G-1 shows temporary traffic control regulatory signs with varying amounts of text but no maximum word requirement; [Image 3] Table 2B-1 evidence relates to minimum sign sizes, not word counts; [Image 4] Table 6G-1 lists sign sizes for TTC zones, not message length limits. Citations: - Section 2L.05 Standard §4 (p.515) - Figure 2A-1 (p.48) - Figure 6G-1 (p.794) - Table 2B-1 (p.67) - Table 6G-1 (p.793)
